title: Marvel Limits Early Doomsday Screenings to Protect Spoilers
excerpt:
Marvel will withhold Avengers: Doomsday from early awards screenings.
The strategy affects BAFTA and Golden Globe prospects but leaves an Oscar route.
body_md:
Marvel Studios is prioritizing secrecy around Avengers: Doomsday by withholding the film from awards voting groups ahead of its world premiere. The Los Angeles premiere is scheduled for December 14, 2026, followed by the nationwide theatrical release on December 18.

The decision creates significant awards-season complications. Preliminary Oscar shortlist voting runs from December 7 through December 11, with shortlists announced on December 15. Most voters will therefore have limited opportunities to evaluate the film before those deadlines.

Visual effects remains a potential avenue for Academy recognition. Under the branch's rules, excerpts can be provided in certain circumstances when a complete film is unavailable. The report confirms that Marvel submitted the film and required materials to relevant Academy branches, but whether the visual effects committee received a full screening or excerpts remains unclear.

BAFTA and the Golden Globes present greater obstacles. Doomsday will not be available through BAFTA's viewing platform, while Golden Globe film voting closes on December 4. According to the report, those circumstances effectively remove the film from consideration for both awards this cycle. The Actor Awards remain a possibility because nomination voting begins on December 14.

There is precedent for a major December release succeeding at the Oscars despite a late premiere. Spider-Man: No Way Home earned a visual effects nomination under a similar release schedule. With Robert Downey Jr. returning as Doctor Doom and an ensemble spanning the Avengers, Fantastic Four and X-Men, Marvel appears determined to preserve the theatrical experience. The eventual Oscar outcome remains uncertain.
